sentences.text: Author: Tirthankar Ghosh Bench: Tirthankar Ghosh

In Re: An application for Bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Dismissed Procedure,
1973/under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 filed in connection with Ramnagar Police Station Case No.24 of 2022 dated 15.02.2022 under Sections 363, 365, 366A, 368,
370, 372, 376D, 376(2)(n), 120 B of the Indian Penal Code, Section 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act and Section 6 of the POCSO Act;
Kakali Mondal @ Taposhi @ Buri @ Boudi Versus The State of West Bengal & Anr.
Mr. Deepak Prahladka Ms. Reshmi Khatun.
...for the petitioner.
Mr. Subhomoy Bhattacharjee Mr. Akash Ganguly.
...for the State.
Learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody for more than four years and till date the court could not pronounce its verdict.

Learned advocate, therefore,
submits that there has been violation of Article 22(1) of the Constitution of India and Section 47 of the BNSS, 2023, as such, the arrest being illegal, the petitioner may be released on bail.
Learned advocate appearing for the State submits that earlier arguments were concluded and date was fixed for delivery of judgment when the Presiding Officer was transferred.
Presently, the Presiding Officer has joined.
However, it would take some time to conclude the arguments of the respective parties.
Having considered the reasons assigned earlier by the learned trial court while rejecting the prayer for bail, I do not find any illegality in the same.

However, efforts be exhausted to conclude the arguments within a month from the next date fixed and thereafter within a month from the conclusion of the arguments, learned trial court would pronounce its verdict.
Kakali Mondal @ Taposhi @ Buri @ Boudi vs The State Of West Bengal & Anr
